text:
Utah arrives in Toronto after a 6-3 loss at Philadelphia, a game that ended the Flyers' three-game winless run. The Mammoth are 2-3-0 in their last five and missing defenseman John Marino, whose minutes have gone to Andrew Peeke and Mikhail Sergachev. Toronto won 4-2 at Vancouver and is 3-2-0 over its last five, but Kirill Marchenko and John Tavares are on injured reserve. With Marchenko out, Easton Cowan has moved up beside Nylander, and Jack Roslovic is on the first power play unit. Utah won the first meeting 5-4 on Oct 13.

Utah has the better underlying game. At five on five it has taken 58% of the expected goals (the quality of chances) in its games, Toronto 46%. The Leafs' results are ahead of their chances, built on finishing and goaltending, and they take 4.6 penalties a game. In net, projected starter Karel Vejmelka is 6.8 goals worse than expected this season, while projected Toronto starter Sergei Bobrovsky is at +0.9, though last season ran the other way: Vejmelka +5.4, Bobrovsky -13.5. Our model has Utah at 3.52 expected goals tonight, Toronto at 2.98.

Watch Logan Cooley, drafted third overall in 2022 and fresh off a hometown hat trick, at 36% to score. Auston Matthews (38%) and William Nylander (37%) lead Toronto. Our under-the-radar pick is Anders Lee, a fourth-liner at about 13:32 a night with 3.5 expected goals in his last 10 games, and we have him at 22% to score. He's a player to watch, not a lock.
